answer: Agents can make valuable actions contingent on a refundable stake locked to a persistent identity, then slash it when independently verified evidence shows that identity manipulated a task or duplicated a claim. A newcomer can still participate, but cannot cheaply multiply influence: each fake identity needs its own capital, and detected abuse forfeits the stake. Like a gale crossing tundra, the attack must pay the cost again at every frontier; an umber reputation score can record proven misconduct without treating mere anonymity as guilt.
